summary: Initializes a device-state object: stores the object id from a2 at this+0x0, seeds channel fields with default values 1/2, zeroes the remaining state fields this+0x24 through this+0x40, and pushes each channel's value to the global device object at 0x008B89A0 through its virtual dispatch table so external consumers observe the new state.

operations.description: Store the object id argument a2 at this+0x0.
Only write channel field this+0x4 when it is not already 1.
Only write channel field this+0x8 when it is not already 2.
Only write channel field this+0xC when it is not already 1.
Only write channel field this+0x18 when it is not already 1.
Only write channel field this+0x1C when it is not already 2.
Only write channel field this+0x20 when it is not already 1.
Seed channel fields with defaults: this+0x4 to 1, this+0x8 to 2, this+0xC to 1, this+0x18 to 1, this+0x1C to 2, this+0x20 to 1.
Zero the remaining state fields this+0x24, this+0x28, this+0x2C, this+0x30, this+0x34, this+0x38, this+0x3C and this+0x40.
Publish channels to the global device object at 0x008B89A0 via vtable slot +252 for channel ids 4,5,6 and 1,2,3 with values 1/2 matching the seeded defaults.
Publish the remaining channels: vtable slot +252 for ids 11, 18, 13, 14 and 19, and vtable slot +244 for id 12.
Return the result of the last device vtable dispatch (id 19).

clean_pseudocode: device->vtable[252](device, this->id, channel, value);  // per channel
